summary.en: Group fixed-position values with tuples, unpack them safely, and use hashable tuples as dictionary keys.
summary.bn: টাপলে নির্দিষ্ট অবস্থানের মান রাখো, আনপ্যাক করো এবং উপযুক্ত টাপলকে ডিকশনারির কী হিসেবে ব্যবহার করো।

notes: Tuple packing, starred assignment and the hashability rules used here are available throughout Python 3.10–3.12. A tuple containing a mutable list remains unhashable in each of these versions.

sections.title: Treat a small group as one value
Fixed slots can hold changeable objects
Unpack records and look up coordinates
Match the shape of the group
Do not confuse fixed with deeply frozen
Use tuples to keep a record together

examples.title: Pack and unpack a result
examples.explanationHtml: The comma packs two values into one tuple. Unpacking binds course and mark in order. The trailing comma in (82,) makes a one-item tuple rather than a parenthesized integer.

examples.title: Unpack a flexible middle
examples.explanationHtml: The fixed ends become 60 and 90. A starred target collects the middle into a list. Swapping evaluates the right-hand values first, so no temporary name is needed.

examples.title: Keep tuple slots fixed but edit a contained list
examples.explanationHtml: The tuple still refers to roll 12 and the same list. Appending changes that list rather than replacing a tuple slot. Immutability of the tuple does not freeze everything reachable from it.

examples.title: Look up a seat by coordinate
examples.explanationHtml: The tuple (1, 2) acts as one dictionary key, so the pair identifies a seat. get returns the fallback for an absent coordinate. Dictionaries are key-to-value lookup containers, taught in their own lesson.

practice.title: Swap the endpoints
practice.statementHtml: Read two integers on one line. Use tuple unpacking to swap their bindings, then print the new first and second values separated by one space.
hints: The entire right side is evaluated before either target is assigned.

practice.title: Split a score record
practice.statementHtml: Read at least two integer scores on one line. Unpack the first and last with a starred middle. Print the endpoints on one line and the middle sum on the next.
hints: The starred target is a list, including when there are no middle values.

practice.title: Mirror a coordinate
practice.statementHtml: Read integer row and column on one line. Pack them into a tuple and print the original tuple. Then print a new tuple with the positions exchanged.
hints: Create another tuple; do not assign to a tuple item.

practice.title: Seat status lookup
practice.statementHtml: Read a row and column on one line. Seats (1,1) and (1,2) are occupied; every other coordinate is free. Store these tuple keys in a dictionary and print occupied or free.
hints: Use a coordinate tuple as one key and get with a fallback.

quiz.prompt: Which type does a parenthesized integer have without a comma?
quiz.explanation: Parentheses group the integer expression; the comma creates the singleton tuple.

quiz.prompt: What type and contents does starred unpacking give the middle?
quiz.explanation: The starred target collects all values between the fixed first and last targets into a list.

quiz.prompt: What can change inside an immutable tuple?
quiz.explanation: The list object changes; the tuple still holds the same two references.

quiz.prompt: Which value can serve as a dictionary key?
quiz.explanation: Integers and strings are hashable; a tuple containing a list is not.

quiz.prompt: What happens when two targets unpack a three-item tuple?
options: The first target receives two values
quiz.explanation: Without a starred target, unpacking requires exactly as many values as targets.

quiz.prompt: Which syntax creates an empty tuple?
quiz.explanation: Empty parentheses create the empty tuple; a comma alone is not valid here.

options: Its stored references cannot be replaced, added or removed
Its items must share a type
quiz.explanation: Immutability fixes tuple slots; nested objects keep their own behavior.

quiz.prompt: When is a tuple a good choice for a course result?
options: When arbitrary items need frequent insertion
When every lookup should use a text key
When positions have fixed roles such as course code and mark
quiz.explanation: A tuple expresses a fixed group; a list better expresses a changing collection.

quiz.prompt: How does point[1:] behave on a tuple?
quiz.explanation: Slicing a tuple keeps the sequence type and does not edit the original.

quiz.prompt: Why can equal coordinate tuples retrieve the same dictionary value?
options: They must be the identical object
Dictionary keys use equality and compatible hashes
The dictionary unpacks them into two keys
quiz.explanation: Equal hashable tuples represent one logical key even when created separately.

keyPoints.en: Commas create tuples, including one-item tuples.
keyPoints.bn: কমা দিয়ে টাপল তৈরি হয়; এক মানের টাপলেও কমা লাগে।

keyPoints.en: Unpacking matches values to targets in order.
keyPoints.bn: আনপ্যাকিংয়ে ক্রম অনুযায়ী টার্গেটে মান বসে।

keyPoints.en: A starred target collects extra values in a list.
keyPoints.bn: স্টার দেওয়া টার্গেটে বাড়তি মানগুলো লিস্ট হিসেবে জমা হয়।

keyPoints.en: Tuple immutability does not freeze a contained list.
keyPoints.bn: টাপল অপরিবর্তনীয় হলেও তার ভেতরের লিস্ট বদলাতে পারে।

keyPoints.en: A tuple key needs every contained item to be hashable.
keyPoints.bn: কী হিসেবে টাপল ব্যবহার করতে তার প্রতিটি মান হ্যাশযোগ্য হতে হয়।

examQuestions.question: Why can (1, 2) be a dictionary key while (1, [2]) cannot?
examQuestions.answerHtml: The first tuple contains only hashable integers. The second contains an unhashable list. A tuple needs all of its components to be hashable to serve as a key.

examQuestions.question: Give a, b and c after a, *b, c = (4, 5).
examQuestions.answerHtml: a is 4, b is the empty list [], and c is 5. The fixed targets consume both values, leaving none for the starred target.

examQuestions.question: Pack code CSE101 and mark 75 into a tuple, unpack it and print code followed by mark.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
result = ("CSE101", 75)
course, mark = result
print(course, mark)

The output is CSE101 75. Unpacking assigns the two positions in order.
